entries.title: Shadow of the Ninja
entries.summary: Natsume's 1990 ninja platformer: Iga ninjas Hayate and Kaede infiltrate Emperor Garuda's stronghold in a future US city to assassinate him.
entries.why_it_matters: Supports simultaneous two-player co-op. A planned Game Boy version became Ninja Gaiden Shadow.
entries.gameplay_notes: Hang and move beneath overhangs. The katana and longer-reaching kusarigama upgrade when you collect duplicates and downgrade when you take damage. Shuriken and grenades have limited supplies. A thunderstorm special hits the whole screen but costs half your health.
entries.hltb_note: No NES HLTB entry could be matched (HLTB search is not accessible to automated tools; only Wikidata-linked or title-matched ids were used).

entries.title: Shadowgate
entries.summary: Kemco's NES version, published by Seika, of ICOM's 1987 MacVenture: the last hero-king explores Castle Shadowgate to stop the Warlock Lord from summoning the Behemoth.
entries.why_it_matters: Its NES success led Kemco to port the other MacVentures (Déjà Vu, Uninvited). It's famous for its countless, darkly funny deaths.
entries.gameplay_notes: Point-and-click puzzles using verb commands. Torches burn out, acting as a time limit, and when the last goes out you die. Almost any wrong action is fatal. The NES version has a hint feature and continues from the room where you died.

difficulty.reason: Trial-and-error puzzles with frequent instant deaths and a torch time limit.

entries.hltb_note: HLTB entry exists but has no NES-specific times (other platforms only); not used.
entries.content_notes: Graphic text descriptions of deaths remain even in the NES version.

entries.title: Tecmo Super Bowl
entries.summary: Tecmo's 1991 sequel, the first game licensed by both the NFL and the NFLPA: all 28 NFL teams with real players, using 1990 season rosters.
entries.why_it_matters: Has a long-running cult following, with tournaments and annual fan roster updates. It is regularly named one of the best and most influential sports games.
entries.gameplay_notes: Full season with statistics tracking and NFL records, and expanded playbooks. Some stars appear as 'QB Bills' and similar because they weren't in the NFLPA deal.
